_note: AI-drafted Call to Worship — pending Wilson's curation.

registers.label: Spare
lines: While we were still far off, God saw us and ran.
We are pilgrims on the way to the cross.
We squandered the inheritance and came home in rags.
The Father has put a robe around our shoulders.
The calf is killed; the feast is ready.
We were lost, and we are found. Come, let us worship.

registers.label: Immersive
lines: See the father on the road, robe hiked up, running — running while the son is still a long way off.
We are pilgrims on the way to the cross.
You who came home rehearsing your apology, you who fed the pigs and dreamed of bread — the arms are already around you.
We are pilgrims on the way to the cross.
The best robe, the ring, the sandals, the fatted calf — for this child was dead and is alive again.
We are pilgrims on the way to the cross.
So come in from the field, elder and younger alike; the music has started and the table is full.
We are pilgrims on the way to the cross. Amen.

registers.label: Hybrid
lines: While we were far off, the Father ran and threw his arms around us.
Turn us, O God, and we will return.
He puts the best robe on our shoulders and a ring on our hand.
Turn us, O God, and we will return.
We were dead and are alive; come to the feast.
Turn us, O God, and we will return. Amen.
